minutes.headline: Sewer Commission reviewed a FY24 draft budget with a large retained-earnings draw, and chose a lien over Board of Health action on unpaid grease fees.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed the FY24 draft budget, which starts with a deficit covered by retained earnings, and a presentation for the Finance Committee that needs a corrected debt-service slide. It voted on town meeting articles and minutes, and discussed the pumping-station contract RFP, a clerical position, grease trap non-compliance, and a new inflow/infiltration float sensor. For the unpaid non-compliance invoice, members leaned toward a municipal lien rather than involving the Board of Health.

contention.sides: One commissioner favoured involving the Board of Health; another commissioner opposed that and urged a pre-lien, and a third leaned toward the lien.

what_happened.line: The commission reviewed a draft FY24 budget that opens with a deficit, covered by a draw from retained earnings.
Members leaned toward a municipal lien, not Board of Health action, for an unpaid grease-trap non-compliance invoice; the business manager is to consult the tax collector and town counsel.
A debt service slide in the Finance Committee presentation did not match actual debt service, and the business manager is to correct it.
A motion on the sewer town meeting articles was made, but the outcome was not audible in the recording.
Commissioners are to review a draft pumping-station contract RFP, and staff are to screen assistant business manager applicants and draft a clerk job description.

why_it_matters: The sewer enterprise budget begins FY24 in deficit and relies on retained earnings, so sewer bills and the fund's reserves depend on how that draw is later replenished.
Collecting unpaid grease-trap fees through a property lien would put the charge on the property record, which matters to owners of commercial properties served by the sewer.
watch_next: The next meeting agenda, which is to carry the lien question, the pumping-station RFP review and the budget-versus-actual snapshot.
The corrected debt service slide for the Finance Committee presentation.
